concepts.name: session
concepts.definition: One supervised agent process (Claude Code, Codex, Kimi Code, Grok or a custom CLI) that glimmervoid spawns in a PTY, keyed by a stable UUID and shown on the dashboard

concepts.name: worktree
concepts.definition: The git worktree glimmervoid creates for one session from the integration branch, so concurrent sessions never share a working tree

concepts.name: lane
concepts.definition: A background job glimmervoid runs beside operator sessions on its own schedule (team review, Radar, usage), built as a pure core, an IO-free poller and a thin wiring shell

concepts.name: view
concepts.definition: A primary dashboard surface the operator switches between (Focus, Settings, Trace, Usage and the lane tabs, plus Boards on the phone), or one session's rendering inside it, its face (Terminal or the Board pane in Focus)

concepts.name: team
concepts.definition: The operator's GitHub team, whose open pull requests the team review lane reviews and lists in Reviews, Team

concepts.name: attention
concepts.definition: Which sessions need the operator now, ranked from their status, and the surfaces that show it (the Board attention row, the rail readout, notifications)

concepts.name: waiting
concepts.definition: The session status meaning the agent stopped and needs the operator, derived from hook events or the OSC-0 title

concepts.name: sane yolo
concepts.definition: Glimmervoid's session protection: the Safety Net hooks that refuse risky commands and credential reads in sessions and lanes; accident protection, never a sandbox

concepts.name: operator
concepts.definition: The one carbon unit who runs glimmervoid and its dashboard and answers its sessions

concepts.name: agent adapter
concepts.definition: The per-agent module (first-class: Claude Code, Codex, Kimi Code; best effort: Grok, custom CLI) that tells glimmervoid how to spawn, resume and read the status of one agent kind

concepts.name: visions
concepts.definition: The retired editor lane that commented on documents open in the VS Code extension; it survives only in the changelog's history

concepts.name: radar
concepts.definition: The PostHog auto-fix lane that investigates PostHog errors in a session and writes an HTML report

concepts.name: operator config
concepts.definition: Glimmervoid's own settings file, config.json under the operator's glimmervoid home, whose shape is the config schema in shared/contracts/config.ts

concepts.name: monitoring
concepts.definition: The status the dashboard shows for a working session whose turn has ended while its background tasks or sub-agents are still running

concepts.name: starting
concepts.definition: The status the dashboard shows while a session sets up its worktree and boots its agent, until the agent's first turn begins

concepts.name: failed
concepts.definition: A session state: the agent process exited with an error, so the session needs the operator to restart or close it before it can continue.

concepts.name: zen
concepts.definition: A retired experimental dashboard view that showed each live session as a pet in a meadow and staged one session needing the operator at a time; past release notes still name it.

concepts.name: worth a look
concepts.definition: The review panel's short list of change signals an operator can act on: a file another session is changing, a package link into another repository, or a usual partner file left out.

concepts.name: committed
concepts.definition: Changes a session has recorded in commits on its branch, as opposed to edits still only in its worktree.

concepts.name: pairing
concepts.definition: Granting a device access to the remote listener with a single-use link from glimmervoid pair; a paired device has full control as the operator.

concepts.name: experimental
concepts.definition: A Glimmervoid build published from a green push to main as X.Y.Z-next.N under the npm next tag, and the settings that run only on such a build

concepts.name: channel
concepts.definition: The update stream an install follows: release (npm latest) or experimental (the newer of npm next and latest)

concepts.name: copy
concepts.definition: Text an agent or the operator puts on the browser clipboard from a terminal, offered through the Copy to clipboard prompt when the browser blocks the agent's own write.

concepts.name: rescan
concepts.definition: The first-run checklist action that looks again for installed agents and repository roots without a restart.

concepts.name: skip
concepts.definition: An operator choice to pass over a step Glimmervoid would otherwise take, as in skipping permission prompts or the skip-to-main link.

concepts.name: kimi code
concepts.definition: Moonshot's Kimi Code CLI, one of the agent CLIs glimmervoid supervises through its kimi agent adapter

concepts.name: antigravity cli
concepts.definition: Google's Antigravity CLI (agy), one of the agent CLIs glimmervoid supervises through its antigravity agent adapter

concepts.name: question
concepts.definition: An agent's request for the operator's answer (Claude Code AskUserQuestion, Codex request_user_input, Kimi Code AskUserQuestion), carried as the question kind of a session's ConversationApproval and putting the session in waiting until answered

concepts.name: community question
concepts.definition: A question a member of the public asked on a watched community source (posthog.com/questions or an allowlisted Discord channel) that the Community tab tracks, researches and drafts a reply for, which the operator posts by hand.

concepts.name: discord
concepts.definition: A community source: the PostHog Discord server, read through the Discord events PostHog already captures, limited to the channel names the operator allowlists.

concepts.name: community
concepts.definition: The experimental lane and dashboard tab that watches community sources for new community questions and drafts researched answers the operator posts by hand

concepts.name: connect
concepts.definition: Link a session to a whiteboard so it is told what others changed on the board; the connection lives on the board record

concepts.name: running
concepts.definition: The session status meaning the agent is mid-turn and working, derived from hook events or the OSC-0 title

concepts.name: boards
concepts.definition: A shared whiteboard of boxes, wires, frames, notes and plan units that sessions and the operator draw together, opened in a Board pane beside a session's terminal in Focus and listed as rows under its project in the Focus rail (also: board)

concepts.name: pull request
concepts.definition: A GitHub pull request a session is linked to, shown on its card and in Reviews

concepts.name: trust
concepts.definition: An agent CLI's own record that a folder may run its project config and tools without asking, such as Kimi Code's Trust this folder? dialog, which Glimmervoid pre-grants for the sessions it spawns

concepts.name: verdict
concepts.definition: A community research run's confidence in its draft (HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW or FAILED); only a finished HIGH run with a draft notifies

concepts.name: docs
concepts.definition: Text files a session hands the operator with glimmervoid edit to read, edit and save back in the doc editor; its Docs button is hidden from the session header until the feature is ready

concepts.name: markup
concepts.definition: The doc editor's red pen mode, which shows a doc's CriticMarkup edits as teacher-style marks the operator accepts, rejects or adds to

concepts.name: dismiss
concepts.definition: Close a review item on the operator's own pull request with a typed reason, posted as a reply on each of its threads before they are resolved; also clear a session's status as seen (user_dismiss), which takes Complete to Idle and Waiting back to Running

concepts.name: handled
concepts.definition: The list on one of the operator's own pull requests of review items already dismissed or sent to a session, by hand or by a rule, each with Undo

concepts.name: undo
concepts.definition: The Handled list control that reopens a review item, unresolving its thread on GitHub, and keeps rules from acting on it again

concepts.name: fix
concepts.definition: A change that corrects an operator-visible defect, landed as a fix-type commit with a CHANGELOG entry

concepts.name: secretive
concepts.definition: Secretive, a macOS app that keeps SSH keys in the Secure Enclave and serves them through its own agent socket, one of the agent app sockets the commit signer tries

concepts.name: pack
concepts.definition: A folder with a pack.json that adds PR flows, color themes or sandboxed HTML panels to Glimmervoid once the operator approves it in the Packs tab

concepts.name: question manager
concepts.definition: The rule-driven answerer that replies to a session's question from the operator's questionManager rules and passes every other question to the operator as a waiting question

concepts.name: gemini cli
concepts.definition: Google's Gemini CLI, an agent CLI glimmervoid supervises through its gemini agent adapter, with hook status from a generated GEMINI_CLI_HOME

concepts.name: qwen code
concepts.definition: Alibaba's Qwen Code CLI, an agent CLI glimmervoid supervises through its qwen agent adapter, with hook status from a generated QWEN_HOME

concepts.name: copilot cli
concepts.definition: GitHub's Copilot CLI, an agent CLI glimmervoid supervises through its copilot agent adapter, with hook status from a generated COPILOT_HOME

concepts.name: queued
concepts.definition: The Reviews group for a team review waiting its turn for the review lane, before an agent starts on it

concepts.name: parked
concepts.definition: The Reviews group for a pull request set aside with no action left: a discarded team review or one of the operator's own drafts, collapsed by default

concepts.name: host
concepts.definition: A machine running Glimmervoid; linked hosts, other such machines this dashboard reached over an ssh tunnel, are retired and named only in history

concepts.name: watcher
concepts.definition: The always-on process that runs no sessions, dashboard or lane logic: it runs the probes the server sends it and nudges the server when one changes; it runs inside a doorman, the local one the server starts or one on its own box so the server can sleep

concepts.name: server
concepts.definition: The Glimmervoid Node.js background process on the operator's machine that supervises sessions, serves the dashboard and runs the lanes

concepts.name: reviewing now
concepts.definition: The Reviews column holding the Your turn pull requests the operator pulled in to work on, capped by the Reviewing now limit; the rest of Your turn shows as Ready

concepts.name: card
concepts.definition: A session's tile on the dashboard: its terminal with the header, status and Session actions menu, which Focus centers and the phone borrows; also a Reviews item or a whiteboard media box shown the same way

concepts.name: prompt
concepts.definition: The operator's message that starts an agent turn in a session, and the agent's request for input or permission (a permission prompt) that ends one

concepts.name: turn
concepts.definition: One agent work cycle in a session, from the prompt that starts it to the stop that ends it; Your turn is also the Reviews group of items waiting on the operator

concepts.name: settings
concepts.definition: The dashboard's Settings view, whose sections (Appearance, Sane YOLO, Packs, Vault, Server and others) edit the operator config

concepts.name: focus
concepts.definition: The desktop Focus view: a left roster rail with one pill per session grouped by project, and one large center holding the selected session's terminal and Board panes; the phone Board is labelled Focus

concepts.name: layout
concepts.definition: One of the dashboard's two first-class shells, desktop or phone, chosen by decideLayout from pointer and viewport; also the arrangement of Focus panes and a board's laid-out geometry

concepts.name: control
concepts.definition: The control WebSocket (/control), the JSON channel between the server and every dashboard that carries session, board and review messages, beside the data WebSocket of raw PTY bytes; its handlers form the server's control plane

concepts.name: home
concepts.definition: A folder that holds an agent's or Glimmervoid's own state: the glimmervoid home (~/.glimmervoid), the per-agent homes Glimmervoid generates under its agent-homes folder (a Kimi Code, Codex, Gemini, Qwen or Copilot home), or the watcher home

concepts.name: action
concepts.definition: An operator command offered on a thing in the dashboard: a session action in the card's Session actions menu, or a PR action from prFlows.prActions shown as a button on a pull request

concepts.name: report
concepts.definition: A written result handed back to the operator: a Radar investigation's HTML report, the report a PR action sends when it finishes, or the Usage tab's report

concepts.name: review
concepts.definition: An agent's pass over a pull request in the team review lane, drafted for the operator to post, or a GitHub review on the operator's own pull request; the Reviews tab queues both

concepts.name: draft
concepts.definition: A team review or community answer an agent prepared and the operator has not posted yet; on GitHub, a draft pull request, which Reviews parks when it is the operator's own

concepts.name: unit
concepts.definition: A plan step on a whiteboard: a unit element with a status (planned, building, landed) whose wires give the build order

concepts.name: parent
concepts.definition: The session that spawned another through the session tool; its child talks only to it, and closing a child that holds unlanded work is refused until the parent has it pushed or discards it

concepts.name: signal
concepts.definition: A structural fact a session's status is derived from (an agent hook event or an OSC-0 title glyph, never screen content), and the small status badge signal.ts draws from it

concepts.name: comment
concepts.definition: A review comment on a pull request: a GitHub thread the operator can send to a session or dismiss, or a line comment in a team review draft

concepts.name: base
concepts.definition: The branch or commit a worktree or pull request builds on: the base branch a session worktree is cut from and rebased onto, or a pull request's base, and the diff base a review compares against

concepts.name: group
concepts.definition: A named section items are sorted into: one of the six Reviews groups (Your turn, Agent working, Queued, Waiting on others, Done, Parked), a project group of sessions in the roster, or an alert group that folds notifications

concepts.name: link
concepts.definition: A connection Glimmervoid keeps and shows between two things: a session linked to its pull request, or a board card linked to a file in the code session worktree

concepts.name: model
concepts.definition: The model an agent runs, picked per session, per team review or per Arena setup from the agent model catalog Glimmervoid reads from each agent CLI, and the unit Usage breaks spend down by

concepts.name: element
concepts.definition: One drawn thing on a whiteboard (a box, frame, wire or stroke), counted against a board's element limit; a plan step and a note are boxes

concepts.name: frame
concepts.definition: A whiteboard element that encloses a set of boxes under a title

concepts.name: wire
concepts.definition: A whiteboard element drawn as a line from one end to another, each end a box or a free point, with arrowheads at none, one or both ends and a route (elbow around boxes, sharp straight or curved); its direction between plan units gives build order; wire contracts are the separate network shapes in shared/contracts

concepts.name: refusal
concepts.definition: Glimmervoid's typed no to an agent's tool call or route request, answered identically on the MCP endpoint and the /agent route so it cannot reveal live session ids

concepts.name: payload
concepts.definition: The body a structural message carries: an agent hook event's JSON posted to the hook route

concepts.name: workspace
concepts.definition: A session spanning several repositories: a folder of per-repository worktrees (workspaceRepos) with a generated AGENTS.md map, chosen in Add Session

concepts.name: integration branch
concepts.definition: The branch Glimmervoid cuts every session worktree from and rebases onto: the configured integration branch, or each repository's default branch when unset, read from origin

concepts.name: session id
concepts.definition: An identifier of a session: Glimmervoid's own stable UUID that keys a session everywhere, or the agent CLI's own conversation id that auto-resume captures to resume it

concepts.name: agent
concepts.definition: A coding agent CLI Glimmervoid supervises in a session (Claude Code, Codex, Kimi Code first-class; Grok, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Copilot CLI and custom CLIs best effort), read through its agent adapter

concepts.name: status
concepts.definition: A session's derived state (starting, running, waiting, idle, complete, failed and the rest), computed from structural signals by the session state machine and shown by the status badge

concepts.name: idle
concepts.definition: The session status for an agent at rest with nothing for the operator to do, reached on a starting session's first output or when the operator dismisses a Complete

concepts.name: complete
concepts.definition: The session status after an agent finishes a turn (task_complete from running, waiting or idle, or a compaction restore); it holds until the operator dismisses it, which the dashboard does on its own 3 s after the operator watches it finish, and new output or a prompt leaves it

concepts.name: ready
concepts.definition: A state a thing reaches when it needs the operator next: an agent title showing the idle glyph, a team review draft Ready to post, a plan Ready for review, or a Your turn pull request in the Reviews Ready column, not pulled into Reviewing now

concepts.name: terminal
concepts.definition: A session's live PTY screen rendered with xterm.js in the browser, its Terminal tab and pane in Focus and its Terminal screen on the phone; a headless copy on the server keeps its screen

concepts.name: chat
concepts.definition: The experimental Chat view of a session, the alternative to its terminal: the conversation drawn from trace records, with held questions and permission prompts answered and prompts sent over the control channel while the agent stays on its PTY

concepts.name: dashboard
concepts.definition: The browser app Glimmervoid serves on loopback, where the operator watches and steers sessions across its views, on desktop or phone

concepts.name: phone
concepts.definition: The phone layout of the dashboard: a bottom nav with the Board (labelled Focus), Terminal and the phone-only Boards screen, then a More button whose screens hold the remaining views

concepts.name: usage
concepts.definition: The usage tracking lane and its Usage tab: tokens, cost, plan limits and pace per agent and model, read from agent transcripts on this machine

concepts.name: trace
concepts.definition: The Session Trace: a per-session record of hook events, title signals and state transitions the Trace view shows on request, so a status decision can be read after the fact

concepts.name: detection
concepts.definition: Status detection: deriving each session's status from structural signals (agent hooks plus the OSC-0 title fallback), never from screen content

concepts.name: notification
concepts.definition: An alert Glimmervoid raises for a session that needs the operator, through browser notifications and Telegram, with its own lifecycle state machine

concepts.name: factory
concepts.definition: The retired Factory tab and factory lanes that dispatched Coherence tickets to sessions; removed with the knowledge graph and now named only in history

concepts.name: mill
concepts.definition: The retired context mill, which distilled context packs and Long-Term Memory for sessions; named now only in the changelog

concepts.name: headroom
concepts.definition: Free memory under Glimmervoid's memory limit that the memory gate reads before each automatic session start, shown in the debug health panel; also Headroom, a third-party proxy whose integration was removed

concepts.name: issues
concepts.definition: The retired Issues tab, which listed GitHub issues and opened a session from one; removed with its lane and now named only in history

concepts.name: remote
concepts.definition: Remote access: the always-on remote listener (config remote), behind pairing, that lets a paired device or a doorman reach the server from another machine

concepts.name: shown
concepts.definition: A file an agent showed the operator with the show tool, which now lands as a card on a whiteboard the session is connected to; the retired Shown button and page that once listed such files are gone (0.52.2)

concepts.name: shell
concepts.definition: A session kind that runs the operator's login shell on the Glimmervoid machine instead of an agent, offered in Add Session

concepts.name: coder
concepts.definition: Coder, the remote development platform whose devboxes can host Glimmervoid; remote Coder sessions and Glimmervoid's Coder activity reporting are retired and named only in history

concepts.name: rule
concepts.definition: An operator-written condition and action Glimmervoid applies on its own: a question manager rule that answers a question, or a prFlows rule that acts on a pull request; the brand bible's named design rules are a separate sense

concepts.name: plan
concepts.definition: An agent's proposed approach before it builds: drawn as plan steps on a board, or a Claude Code plan-mode plan the operator approves in the session's own terminal, where the card shows Plan ready

concepts.name: plan review
concepts.definition: The retired dashboard feature that held Claude Code plan approvals on a session card's plan face; named only in the changelog's history, since plans now go through boards and plan-mode approvals answer in the terminal

concepts.name: core
concepts.definition: A pure decision module (session/core, server/core or a *-core file) that does no IO, imports no Session and reads no clock, wrapped by a thin IO shell

concepts.name: note
concepts.definition: A whiteboard box with shape note: a note card in an optional tone, whose author field names the agent or operator that wrote it so the card shows from <author>; also the git note Glimmervoid attaches to a session commit under refs/notes/glimmervoid

concepts.name: ephemeral
concepts.definition: A lane or child session that runs once in a throwaway folder and is removed when it ends, such as a team review or community run, inside the ephemeral lane write boundaries

concepts.name: task title
concepts.definition: The short title Glimmervoid derives from a session's prompts and the agent's own title, which names the session and feeds the automatic namer

concepts.name: benchmarks
concepts.definition: The retired benchmarks lane (formerly the Bench tab), folded into Arena: review cases and recall scoring replace it; the name survives only in the changelog, the benchmarks config key a migration drops, the old suite folders under ~/.glimmervoid/benchmarks whose cases Arena still lists, and the Arena view's internal id

concepts.name: resume
concepts.definition: Start a session's agent again on its earlier conversation by its agent session id; auto-resume does this at boot for sessions that were live when Glimmervoid stopped

concepts.name: restart
concepts.definition: Start a session's agent process again in place, fresh or resuming its conversation; Restart server replaces the running Glimmervoid server with its current version

concepts.name: doctor
concepts.definition: The glimmervoid doctor command that checks the operator's setup, such as PATH, and says what to fix

concepts.name: golgari
concepts.definition: One of Glimmervoid's built-in dashboard color themes, picked in Settings, Appearance

concepts.name: midnight
concepts.definition: One of Glimmervoid's built-in dashboard color themes, picked in Settings, Appearance

concepts.name: phyrexian
concepts.definition: One of Glimmervoid's built-in dashboard color themes, picked in Settings, Appearance

concepts.name: compleated
concepts.definition: One of Glimmervoid's built-in dashboard color themes, picked in Settings, Appearance

concepts.name: conversation
concepts.definition: An agent's own transcript in a session, kept by the agent CLI under its session id, which resume and restart continue; the retired Conversation view once rendered it as chat

concepts.name: record
concepts.definition: A stored entry Glimmervoid keeps about something: a JSONL line of a session recording (header, data, hook, state, decision, input, resize or footer), a Session Trace record (TraceRecord), a board record that holds its connections, or an agent CLI's own trust record; Coherence journal records and design records under docs/ are records too

concepts.name: history
concepts.definition: Past entries a surface keeps and shows over time: the Usage tab's History rows, a Radar issue's recent occurrence points (one per poll, capped at 24), the session card's History list of earlier manager decisions, and the phone's browser history entries per screen level; in prose, also the project's past as the changelog tells it

concepts.name: dead
concepts.definition: As in dead end: Coherence's reading of a component whose defects keep returning after site fixes (DEAD END in spec --check), quoted in this project's journal practice records; elsewhere ordinary English

concepts.name: arena
concepts.definition: The dashboard view where the operator races one prompt across 2 to 5 agent setups, each in its own worktree from the same commit, and a judge ranks the contestants that changed something; a race started from a review case instead has each contestant review that pull request's reviewed commit and ranks them by recall against its reviewers' comments

concepts.name: ws
concepts.definition: The ws npm package, the WebSocket library the server runs the control and data WebSockets on; named in dependency notes and changelog entries

concepts.name: tailwindcss
concepts.definition: The tailwindcss npm package, the Tailwind CSS compiler that builds the dashboard stylesheet through its Vite plugin; named in dependency notes and changelog entries

properties.side: The left, right, top or bottom of a box: where a box placed near another sits (near.side) and where a wire leaves or enters a box (fromSide, toSide); elsewhere (server-side, side by side, a side panel) ordinary English

concepts.name: box
concepts.definition: The solid element of a whiteboard: it carries a title with an optional icon, lines, a place (a point, near another box, aside in the stack right of the drawing, or plan in the build-order band), one of six shapes (box, decision, ellipse, note, icon or device) and optionally media, a width and a step; borderless null takes the shape default, so an icon or device box draws bare; a plan step is a box with a step, an icon box (shape icon) draws its icon large and holds no lines or media, and a device box (shape device) draws a catalog device with its media on the screen and holds no lines; elsewhere (a message box, a remote box) ordinary English

concepts.name: transitions
concepts.definition: The moves a state machine allows, held in one frozen table per machine (session/core/state-machine.ts, shared/state-transitions.ts) and written only by that machine's owner module

concepts.name: teardown
concepts.definition: Ending or restarting a session's agent process (a pending restart, a pending finish-and-merge, or removal), held in one Teardown value moved only by decideTeardown in session/core/session-teardown.ts

concepts.name: outcome
concepts.definition: What a finished operation reports back: a worktree merge's outcome (merged, parked or refused) that becomes the merge status, or a review run's outcome (a draft or an error) that the team review poller settles

concepts.name: icon
concepts.definition: A small picture: on a whiteboard, a glyph from the vendored Lucide catalog (shared/whiteboard-icons.ts) drawn before a box title or line text, or large on a box with shape icon; elsewhere an agent icon, status icon or button glyph on the dashboard

concepts.name: device
concepts.definition: A machine the operator reaches the dashboard from (a paired remote device under remote mode); on a whiteboard, a catalog device (phone, tablet, laptop, desktop or browser, shared/whiteboard-devices.ts) a box with shape device draws around its media

concepts.name: live session
concepts.definition: A session the server still holds in one of its session maps (an operator config session, an agent-spawned session or a lane session), whatever its status and whether its agent is running or has exited, until it is torn down or removed; branch and worktree cleanup, uploads and session temp folders keep what a live session owns; not the running status, which means mid-turn

concepts.name: project
concepts.definition: The repository a session works in, named by the session's configured project path; a whiteboard belongs to one project, the path of the session that created it or first used it

concepts.name: theme
concepts.definition: A named dashboard color palette (chrome and state colors) picked per browser in Settings > Appearance; Glimmer is the default, Glimmer Light, Phyrexian, Midnight, Golgari, Compleated and the rest are alternatives, and a pack can add more

concepts.name: glimmer
concepts.definition: The default dashboard theme: violet-tinted graphite surfaces with a vivid violet accent; Glimmer Light is its light counterpart

concepts.name: graphite
concepts.definition: The neutral color family of the Glimmer theme: its near-black surfaces (Graphite, Card, Header and Inset Graphite) tinted toward violet

concepts.name: paper
concepts.definition: Paper, the Glimmer brand-bible name for the headings color --text-head; also the bg-card paper of the doc editor's Markup mode

concepts.name: light
concepts.definition: A theme mode: a light theme (Glimmer Light, Compleated, PostHog Light) puts dark text on pale surfaces, and the terminal takes ANSI_HUES_BY_MODE.light colors for it

concepts.name: allow
concepts.definition: The operator's answer on a secret request card that saves each named secret's vault reference for the session's project, so later requests for it need no card; Deny is the other answer

concepts.name: vault companion
concepts.definition: The retired glimmervoid vault process that read approved secrets from 1Password over a WebSocket to the server; removed when secrets moved to the pinned fnox helper, and now named only in history, the migration that drops vault.host, vault.port and vault.token, and the boot cleanup of its connection file (also: companion)

concepts.name: connection
concepts.definition: A live WebSocket between two Glimmervoid parts, such as a dashboard's control or data WebSocket to the server; a dropped one is retried with backoff

concepts.name: pane
concepts.definition: One window in the Focus center (the terminal, the board or a shell), each with the same header that drags it onto another pane's edge to rearrange the split

concepts.name: drop
concepts.definition: Letting go of a dragged row or title bar over a target in the dashboard, such as a board row on a session row to open a split

concepts.name: split
concepts.definition: A session with a board, a shell, or both open beside it in Focus, shown as one item in the rail; each session has at most one board and one shell, and each board or shell is in at most one split

concepts.name: probe
concepts.definition: One GitHub or PostHog read the server compiles from exactly what a lane already polls and the watcher runs on an interval, hashing the answer and never parsing it

concepts.name: probe set
concepts.definition: The whole list of probes the server sends the watcher, with a revision that changes whenever any probe does

concepts.name: nudge
concepts.definition: The watcher's signed note to the server that one probe's answer changed, started failing or recovered; it carries no response data, and the lane that owns the probe runs its own poll

concepts.name: link secret
concepts.definition: The random secret in ~/.glimmervoid/secrets/watcher-link.key, which the doorman reads through the path its tenant table names, from which each direction of the watcher link derives its own signing key; never shown in settings

concepts.name: answer field
concepts.definition: The one top-level JSON field of a probe's answer, such as results, that the watcher hashes alone, so per-run fields beside it never nudge

concepts.name: attention note
concepts.definition: A report Glimmervoid itself raises on a session (a kept child worktree, the child or self wake limit, a failed wake), one slot per origin, shown as a card chip and a quiet notification that never moves the session to waiting; cleared by the operator's next prompt or a dismiss

concepts.name: session name
concepts.definition: A session's display name for its area of work, stable across its steps, shown in the rail; never part of the task title or a board title

concepts.name: security
concepts.definition: Protection of the operator's machine, secrets and sessions; a release whose notes carry a Security section fixes a vulnerability, which the update check surfaces as a security notice

concepts.name: jev
concepts.definition: Jev (typesafe-ai/jev), a decision model reached through Vercel AI Gateway that picks, orders and places prebuilt json-render component candidates; named only in the docs/search-builds-the-view.md product outline

concepts.name: search
concepts.definition: Finding settings by text: the Settings view's search box and glimmervoid settings search rank settings by title first, then keywords, section, key path, option labels and description, and link as #settings?q=; the unbuilt docs/search-builds-the-view.md outline also names a search bar that composes a view from a query

concepts.name: revision
concepts.definition: One version of something that changes over time: the hash a probe set carries that changes whenever any probe does

concepts.name: secrets
concepts.definition: Credentials a session needs by name (API keys, tokens): the operator approves each on the session's secret request card, Glimmervoid reads its value from the operator's password manager vault set in Settings, Vault, writes it to the session's env file and masks it everywhere it shows; Settings, Vault lists the approvals (also: secret)

concepts.name: vault
concepts.definition: The feature that keeps the secrets agents may read: Settings, Vault holds the password manager vault to look in with Test connection, each project's approved secrets with revoke, and the GitHub read token lanes use; glimmervoid need and the MCP secrets tool are its other surfaces

concepts.name: guardrails
concepts.definition: The retired name of Sane YOLO, kept only where old data still carries it: the legacy guardrails config key and its migrations, the guardrails-temp folder and the retired guardrails folders swept at startup

concepts.name: review case
concepts.definition: A frozen pull request review Arena can race on: the reviewed and base commits, the changed files, and the reviewers' comments as reference defects, mined from a repository's merged pull requests into ~/.glimmervoid/review-cases/<owner>/<repo>, or kept from an old benchmarks suite's cases folder

concepts.name: app
concepts.definition: The Glimmervoid GitHub App whose private key only the doorman holds; it mints read-only installation tokens scoped to a hosted tenant's repositories

concepts.name: secret manager
concepts.definition: Google Cloud Secret Manager, where the GitHub App private key lives; the doorman reads its current alias at runtime

concepts.name: hint card
concepts.definition: The retired Sessions setting (hintCards) that showed feature tips on the dashboard; folded into Usage, Your day, and a config migration drops the key; the name survives in the changelog and the old settings link that now opens Your day (also: hint)

concepts.name: keyboard
concepts.definition: The phone's on-screen soft keyboard that types into a session's terminal, opened by tapping the terminal and opened or closed by the Keyboard key in the phone key strip

concepts.name: reload
concepts.definition: Loading the dashboard browser page again, which starts a fresh page from the server; it does not lift Chrome's graphics block after repeated graphics card resets, which only quitting and reopening the browser does; also a running process reading a watched file again in place, such as config.json, the doorman's tenant table or a linked card's file; also reading a session's changes again from its worktree after Changes failed to read them, through the Reload changes button

concepts.name: merged
concepts.definition: A pull request's GitHub state once it lands on its base branch; the Reviews Merged column and an own pull request's Merged stage

concepts.name: end
concepts.definition: One of a wire's two attachment points on a whiteboard, its from end or its to end; the properties panel's Ends section picks the side of its box each attaches to, or auto

concepts.name: backspace
concepts.definition: The keyboard key that deletes the character before the cursor; pressed on an empty line in a whiteboard box's line editor it removes that line and moves to the line above

concepts.name: text
concepts.definition: On a whiteboard, the Text tool (T) that places a borderless box, and the plain line style of a box line beside Code, Bullet and Key and value; elsewhere ordinary English

concepts.name: arrow
concepts.definition: An arrow key (Up, Down, Left or Right), a physical key on desktop or one in the phone key strip; on a whiteboard, a wire as drawn, whose head is its arrowhead, the Arrow tool (A) that draws one, or the Arrow box icon

concepts.name: wake
concepts.definition: A prompt a session schedules with glimmervoid wake (in, at or cron) that Glimmervoid types into that session when due, once it is idle and the operator is not typing; also the line a spawned session's news types into its parent. Both spend one per-session budget of 10 without operator input

concepts.name: reset
concepts.definition: A graphics card reset: the browser takes a board's WebGL context away (lost) and the board gets one back (restored or recreated); after repeated resets Chrome blocks graphics for the site until the browser restarts, and each one is logged as a board-graphics line and a board_graphics_reset event

concepts.name: account
concepts.definition: A signed-in agent login Glimmervoid can run a session under: the machine's own login, or an added account whose folder (agentAccounts[].folder) holds its own credentials and links the rest of the agent's real home; for Claude Code one email can hold several, one per organization

concepts.name: launcher
concepts.definition: A pack launcher: a button a pack declares under launchers (label, project, agent, optional model, effort and cron schedule, first prompt) that starts a session once the operator approves the pack; also the script or function that starts a process, such as the glimmervoid bin launcher or an agent's launch command

concepts.name: shares
concepts.definition: The fractions of a split's space its children take, one per child, adding up to the whole; dragging a divider between two panes moves share from one to the other

concepts.name: repository
concepts.definition: A git checkout a session works in; the dashboard's Add a repository step clones one from GitHub or a pasted URL into a repository root, or adds a folder that holds checkouts

concepts.name: cloud storage
concepts.definition: Google Cloud Storage, where a hosted doorman's state bucket keeps its tenant table, awake ledgers and watcher files

concepts.name: tone
concepts.definition: Whether a notice under the dashboard header is an error (Failed red) or a warning (Needs Input amber); carried as tone on notice_shown telemetry

concepts.name: saved name
concepts.definition: The file name a board media card saves under from the browser's own menus: its source file's name, its uploaded name, or its card title with the media's extension

concepts.name: touch input
concepts.definition: A dashboard that a finger can drive: the phone layout, or any device with a coarse pointer such as a touch tablet, foldable or touchscreen laptop; stamped as data-touch-input on the page, it turns on the touch controls, while a mouse-only desktop has none

concepts.name: android chrome
concepts.definition: Google Chrome on an Android phone or tablet, one of the two phone browsers the dashboard's touch features are built and device-tested for, beside Safari on iPhone

concepts.name: compose bar
concepts.definition: The text field with a Send button the phone Terminal screen once had above the key strip for autocorrect, dictation and paste; removed when the terminal itself took those keyboard features, named only in history

concepts.name: raw typing
concepts.definition: The phone Terminal input mode that typed straight into the PTY with the compose bar hidden; with the compose bar removed it is the only way the phone types, named only in history

concepts.name: selection mirror
concepts.definition: The transparent text layer a long-press lays over a touch Terminal screen, one row per visible terminal row, so the phone draws its own selection handles and Copy menu over the canvas

concepts.name: select sheet
concepts.definition: The full-screen sheet the Select key opens on a touch Terminal screen: the terminal's screen and scrollback as plain text for native selection, with Copy screen and Copy output

concepts.name: touch id
concepts.definition: Touch ID, Apple's fingerprint sign-in that 1Password asks for on each vault read on a Mac; absent on a devbox or in the cloud, where a service account or Connect token stands in

concepts.name: marketing
concepts.definition: The marketing/ folder of the social images and videos that promote Glimmervoid (marketing/social, marketing/video); in older changelog entries, the bundled marketing agent team that the removed Teams feature ran

concepts.name: enable
concepts.definition: The operator action that installs one pack from a pack source or the Glimmervoid examples, unapproved, from the Packs tab's Discover grid

concepts.name: discover
concepts.definition: The Packs tab grid of packs from pack sources and the Glimmervoid examples that are not installed yet

concepts.name: doorman
concepts.definition: The always-on process in front of each tenant's server, run as glimmervoid doorman: it forwards the tenant's dashboard traffic, wakes and stops its host, meters its awake hours and hosts its watcher. It holds a credential only when one of those jobs needs it while the server sleeps: the GitHub App key, the tenant's GitHub connection, each tenant's link secret, and the sealed probe credentials the server sends its watcher (a GitHub read token and a PostHog key). It is not a broker of secrets for sessions or lanes on an awake server, so vault reads, notification tokens and agent logins never move into it

concepts.name: glimmervoid cloud
concepts.definition: The hosted service that runs a Glimmervoid per paying account on its own VM behind the doorman, with sign-in and billing on the account page

concepts.name: board file
concepts.definition: A .glimmerboard file: one board with its media, written by whiteboard export so an operator on another machine opens it as a new board with whiteboard import

concepts.name: managed version
concepts.definition: A Glimmervoid whose release someone other than the operator installs and pins, declared by GLIMMERVOID_MANAGED_BY holding the manager's name; Settings > Updates names the manager and offers no update

concepts.name: register
concepts.definition: To add this host's commit signing key to the connected GitHub account as a signing key, so commits signed with it show as Verified; Register on GitHub is the control that does it

concepts.name: clone
concepts.definition: A copy of a repository that Glimmervoid makes with git clone into the operator's repository folder from the Add a repository step; a clone job is one such copy the server queues, runs, reports progress for and can cancel

concepts.name: rename
concepts.definition: To change the display name of a session or a board in place: double-click, F2 or Enter on a session name, or click on a board title; the stable id never changes

concepts.name: tool lock
concepts.definition: The whiteboard toolbar toggle (Q) that keeps the picked drawing tool after each placement instead of returning to Select

concepts.name: resize handle
concepts.definition: One of the eight squares, four corners and four edges, around a selected whiteboard box or selection that drags to resize it

concepts.name: context menu
concepts.definition: The whiteboard menu a right-click, the Menu key or Shift+F10 opens on the board, holding clipboard, stacking order, align and distribute actions for the selection, or paste, select all and fit on empty board

concepts.name: shortcut
concepts.definition: A key chord that runs a dashboard or whiteboard action, such as Ctrl+] to bring a selection forward, shown beside the action in its menu

concepts.name: style popover
concepts.definition: The whiteboard panel above the properties panel that sets the fill tint, title size, wire tone and wire width of every selected element at once

concepts.name: ellipse
concepts.definition: The oval box shape on a whiteboard (shape ellipse): it holds a title, lines and media like a box and takes a fill tint

concepts.name: eraser
concepts.definition: The whiteboard tool that removes every element a drag crosses, in one undoable step

concepts.name: end handle
concepts.definition: The round handle at each end of a selected whiteboard wire: dragging it onto a box binds that end, dragging it off leaves the end at a free point

concepts.name: hold to lift
concepts.definition: The phone whiteboard gesture: touching and holding a box for about 300 ms selects it and turns the touch into a move drag, where a plain drag would pan

concepts.name: bend point
concepts.definition: A point a whiteboard wire passes through between its ends, stored in order in the wire's via list; on a sharp or curved wire the operator adds one by dragging a leg's midpoint handle and removes one by double-clicking it, and on an elbow wire the bend points are its corners, moved by dragging a segment

concepts.name: rotate handle
concepts.definition: The round handle above a single selected whiteboard box that turns it about its center when dragged, snapping to 15 degree steps with Shift; the box stores the turn as its angle in whole degrees

concepts.name: browser
concepts.definition: The web browser the operator opens the dashboard in, on desktop or phone; it raises native notifications, holds the clipboard and keeps a tab's history

concepts.name: choice
concepts.definition: An option the operator picks among several in a dashboard control, such as an agent, model or effort in Add Session, or a setting value; a project that sets no choice falls back to the default

concepts.name: fixed
concepts.definition: The CHANGELOG section heading under a release that lists operator-visible bugs that release repairs

concepts.name: port
concepts.definition: The TCP port a Glimmervoid listener binds: the local dashboard port, the remote listener port, the local doorman's port named in its port file, or the vault companion's port

concepts.name: clear
concepts.definition: To empty or remove a shown thing: a cleared error message, selection or decision in the dashboard, or an agent conversation reset with /clear, which starts a new agent session id

concepts.name: fire
concepts.definition: To trigger once: a debounced watcher, timer, hook, rule or wake firing its callback, or a false fire when a signal triggers on noise

concepts.name: socket
concepts.definition: A network or IPC endpoint: the control and data WebSockets, a Unix domain socket such as an ssh agent socket, or the vault companion's listener

concepts.name: access
concepts.definition: Permission to read or act on something: a GitHub token's access, a lane's GitHub or PostHog access posture, remote access to the dashboard, or a secret's runtime access

concepts.name: blocks
concepts.definition: Stops an action from going ahead: Sane YOLO blocks a risky command, a failing check blocks a land or spawn; also a whiteboard or Markdown block of content

concepts.name: badge
concepts.definition: A small uppercase state or role label drawn on a card, row or header, such as a session's state badge or a review's owner badge

concepts.name: tag
concepts.definition: A small label chip on a card or header, a git release tag that triggers a build, or a section breadcrumb tag on a search hit

concepts.name: budget
concepts.definition: A cap on a spent resource: GitHub's hourly GraphQL and REST rate limit, a usage token or estimated-cost budget, or a time budget for a lane run

concepts.name: binary
concepts.definition: A standalone executable file, such as the Glimmervoid binary the release workflow builds, the updater beside it, or the Sane YOLO binary named for supervised sessions

concepts.name: alt
concepts.definition: The Alt modifier key; dashboard shortcuts match under Alt outside a Mac and under Cmd on a Mac, and Alt-drag on a board drops a copy

concepts.name: merge
concepts.definition: To land a branch or pull request onto its base, as the Merge, Merge when ready and Keep mergeable actions do; a conflicted merge parks for the agent to resolve

concepts.name: hide
concepts.definition: To take something out of view without deleting it, such as an agent left out of the Add Session picker, a closed panel or a notice

concepts.name: update
concepts.definition: A newer Glimmervoid version and the act of moving to it from Settings, Updates; also any change written to a config, board or pull request

concepts.name: tick
concepts.definition: One beat of a recurring timer, such as the idle-stop tick or a poll; also to check a checkbox, as in ticking repositories to clone

concepts.name: author
concepts.definition: Who wrote something: the GitHub login of a pull request or review comment author, a note's author on a board, or a Discord author shown as a generic member

concepts.name: viewer
concepts.definition: A carbon unit or client watching the dashboard, a board or a video; also the full-size viewer that opens a board picture, video or page

concepts.name: ctrl
concepts.definition: The Control modifier key; board and terminal shortcuts use it, with Cmd standing in on a Mac, and the phone key strip has a sticky Ctrl

concepts.name: layer
concepts.definition: A tier that sits on top of another, such as a board's stacking order, or a mark layer in a design

concepts.name: enter
concepts.definition: The Enter key: it submits a prompt, confirms a dialog, starts a rename on a focused session name and picks a focused row

concepts.name: open
concepts.definition: To bring a thing into view or start it, such as Open a folder, Open in session, opening a board beside a session, or the dashboard opening in a browser on first start

concepts.name: scan
concepts.definition: A pass over a set of things to find what is there, such as the project scan that lists repositories and agents, or a quick read of a list; also the loading mark's scanning brackets

concepts.name: change
concepts.definition: An edit to files a session made, listed in the Changes view of a session's diff from its base; also any settings or board change

concepts.name: cmd
concepts.definition: The Command modifier key on a Mac, which dashboard shortcuts match in place of Alt or Ctrl elsewhere

concepts.name: ui
concepts.definition: The dashboard's user interface: its views, controls, fonts and layouts, as opposed to the server or the agent

concepts.name: add
concepts.definition: To bring a new thing in, such as Add Session, Add a repository, or adding a box to a board

concepts.name: level
concepts.definition: A rank in a hierarchy: a phone screen level with its own history entry, a top-level config key, a log level, or signal-level recording detail

concepts.name: approve
concepts.definition: The operator's GitHub review verdict that a pull request may merge, posted only from the Approve button; also allowing an agent's pack or secret request

concepts.name: check
concepts.definition: A test, CI job or gate that passes or fails, such as a pull request's checks or an update check; also Check by hand, the review list of what to verify manually

concepts.name: keep
concepts.definition: To hold onto something instead of removing it, such as the Keep button for a worktree with unsaved work, or Keep mergeable, which repairs a pull request until it can merge

concepts.name: show
concepts.definition: To put something in front of the operator, such as the show tool that places a file as a board card, or a setting like Show the Community tab

concepts.name: ai
concepts.definition: Artificial intelligence: the coding agents Glimmervoid supervises, as in the For AI Agents section of an instruction file

concepts.name: esc
concepts.definition: The Escape key: it cancels a drag or dialog, clears a pick, and has a sticky key in the phone key strip that interrupts the agent

concepts.name: generated
concepts.definition: Made by a tool rather than written by hand, such as generated files set apart in Changes, or a Generated date header in an AGENTS.md

concepts.name: dependency
concepts.definition: A package the project or a worktree installs, such as a runtime npm dependency listed in AGENTS.md, or a dependency a ticket waits on

concepts.name: markdown
concepts.definition: The Markdown text format: a document the show tool puts on a board and the operator can edit, and the format of every spec and instruction file

concepts.name: remove
concepts.definition: To delete a thing for good, such as Remove for a worktree, a removed setting or feature, or a box taken off a board

concepts.name: close
concepts.definition: To end or dismiss a thing, such as closing a session, a dialog, a panel or a pull request

concepts.name: edit
concepts.definition: To change content in place, such as Edit on a board's Markdown document, the Edit tool of an agent, or editing a setting

concepts.name: gh
concepts.definition: The GitHub CLI, which lanes and setup use for GitHub queries and whose token the GitHub connection can read

concepts.name: new
concepts.definition: Starting a fresh thing, such as New session, New race or a new board

concepts.name: needs
concepts.definition: Requires the operator, as in the Needs you banner and a status such as Needs approval or Needs Input

concepts.name: resolve
concepts.definition: To settle something: resolve a review thread on GitHub, Resolve in session for a conflicted merge, or work out a path or version from config

concepts.name: shift
concepts.definition: The Shift modifier key, which snaps a rotate to 15 degree steps and reverses Tab focus

concepts.name: appearance
concepts.definition: The Settings section for how the dashboard looks: theme, flying animals and other visual choices

concepts.name: set
concepts.definition: To give a setting a value, as in glimmervoid settings set; also a group of things, such as a probe set

concepts.name: discard
concepts.definition: To throw away a session's uncommitted work or a draft; Discard is behind a confirm because it loses work

concepts.name: refresh
concepts.definition: To fetch a value again: a GitHub user token refresh from its refresh token, or reloading a list such as Reviews

concepts.name: send
concepts.definition: To deliver a message: Send on the phone compose bar hands text to the agent, and the server sends notifications and link messages

concepts.name: tab
concepts.definition: The Tab key, which moves focus and has a sticky key in the phone key strip; also a dashboard view tab or a browser tab

concepts.name: back
concepts.definition: To return to the previous screen or level, such as the phone's Back or the browser history entry it pops

concepts.name: cancel
concepts.definition: To stop an action before it completes, such as Cancel on a clone or dialog, or a gate decision that cancels a held ready

concepts.name: save
concepts.definition: To write the operator's edits so they stick, such as Save on a board's Markdown document or a settings change

concepts.name: start
concepts.definition: To begin a session, race or step, as in Start session; also the agent's SessionStart hook that opens a turn

concepts.name: tailscale
concepts.definition: The mesh VPN whose tailscale serve can put the remote listener behind HTTPS, with remote.ownerLogin naming the only Tailscale login it answers

concepts.name: zod
concepts.definition: The schema library that defines every wire and persisted shape in shared/contracts, parsed at each boundary

concepts.name: delete
concepts.definition: To remove something for good, such as Delete my data in Settings, Privacy, a deleted board or a removed line

concepts.name: map
concepts.definition: A JavaScript Map keyed by id, such as a tracker's session map; also the retired Map tab of the review panel or a lean architecture map in an instruction file

concepts.name: privacy
concepts.definition: The Settings section about telemetry and Delete my data, and the rule that no identity or secret leaves the host

concepts.name: request
concepts.definition: An ask from one party to another: an agent's secret or pack request awaiting approval, Request changes on a review, or an HTTP request

concepts.name: stop
concepts.definition: The agent hook event that ends a turn (Stop, SubagentStop), or stopping a session, server or host

concepts.name: workflow
concepts.definition: A sequence of steps run together: workflow rules on pull request events, a GitHub Actions workflow, or the development workflow in AGENTS.md

concepts.name: advanced
concepts.definition: Settings or options set apart for experienced operators, such as an Advanced group in a Settings section

concepts.name: input
concepts.definition: Text or keys sent into a session, as in a terminal's input; Needs Input is the session state that waits on the operator

concepts.name: container
concepts.definition: A Docker container used by the remote-mode test run, or a UI element that lays out its children

concepts.name: diff
concepts.definition: A view of changes between two versions, such as a session's Changes diff from its base or a pull request diff in a review

concepts.name: general
concepts.definition: Not specific to one part: a general shell a lane keeps, or the former General Settings section, now Sessions

concepts.name: origin
concepts.definition: The git remote that is the source of truth for every worktree base, or a browser Origin header the dashboard listeners check

concepts.name: queue
concepts.definition: An ordered list of things awaiting a turn, such as the review queue, the merge queue, the git queue or the clone queue

concepts.name: shared
concepts.definition: Used by more than one party: the shared GitHub store every lane reads, shared constants in shared/, or a board shared between sessions

concepts.name: socat
concepts.definition: A relay utility the retired sandbox runtime once needed on Linux; the install no longer pulls it in

concepts.name: bwrap
concepts.definition: Bubblewrap, the Linux sandbox tool the retired sandbox runtime ran lanes under; the install no longer needs it

concepts.name: paste
concepts.definition: To insert clipboard content, such as Paste on the phone key strip, or pasting text or a picture onto a board

concepts.name: read
concepts.definition: To fetch without changing: a GitHub read token or read-only grant, an agent's Read tool, or a Sane YOLO credential read it blocks

concepts.name: release
concepts.definition: A published Glimmervoid version built from a release tag, and the Release channel of Updates; also a gate decision that releases a held ready

concepts.name: unattended
concepts.definition: Running with no operator present, as in unattended actions now covered by Guardrails and unattended

concepts.name: write
concepts.definition: To change stored state: an agent's Write tool, a config write, or a lane's write boundary

concepts.name: attach
concepts.definition: To add an upload to a session or board, such as Attach on the phone key strip or whiteboard attach; also attaching a terminal to its session's data WebSocket

concepts.name: git
concepts.definition: The version control tool Glimmervoid runs for worktrees, commits, rebases and pushes, through async execFile and one git queue

concepts.name: left
concepts.definition: The Left arrow key, which moves the selection to the previous board column; also left out, as in an agent left out of the picker

concepts.name: option
concepts.definition: The Option modifier key on a Mac, as in Cmd+Option+0; also one of several choices in a design decision or setting

concepts.name: rg
concepts.definition: Ripgrep, the search tool the retired sandbox runtime once needed on Linux

concepts.name: right
concepts.definition: The Right arrow key, which moves the selection to the next board column

concepts.name: ticket
concepts.definition: A unit of work with an id, objective and criteria, as carried by a spec or a retired factory intent

concepts.name: touch
concepts.definition: A finger on a touchscreen, as in phone touch input; also Touch ID on a Mac password manager prompt

concepts.name: boundary
concepts.definition: A line that code or trust may not cross: the trust boundary of the dashboard listeners, a lane's write boundary, or the watcher import boundary

concepts.name: commit
concepts.definition: A git commit a session records on its branch, possibly signed; to make one

concepts.name: common
concepts.definition: Shared by many places, as in the Common Patterns section of an instruction file

concepts.name: credential
concepts.definition: A secret that proves identity, such as a GitHub token, ssh key or password; Sane YOLO blocks agent reads of credentials

concepts.name: develop
concepts.definition: A common git branch name, used as an example of an integration branch that tracks another remote branch

concepts.name: dispatch
concepts.definition: To route an event to its handler, such as the dashboard shortcut dispatch; also the retired glimmervoid dispatch factory command

concepts.name: environment
concepts.definition: The variables a process starts with, scrubbed for every spawned session; also a Coder template environment

concepts.name: export
concepts.definition: To write a thing out for use elsewhere, such as glimmervoid whiteboard export to a .glimmerboard file, or an ES module export

concepts.name: express
concepts.definition: The HTTP server framework the backend runs on, beside ws for WebSockets

concepts.name: first
concepts.definition: The earliest in order, as in the first-run checklist shown before setup is done

concepts.name: global
concepts.definition: Machine-wide rather than per project, such as a global npm install

concepts.name: high
concepts.definition: The top confidence or priority level, such as a High confidence community run that notifies

concepts.name: image
concepts.definition: A picture file, such as one shown on a board, pasted into a session, or labelled [Image #N] in a conversation

concepts.name: ingest
concepts.definition: The retired machine context ingest that fed Visions; an ingest block left in config.json is ignored

concepts.name: install
concepts.definition: To put software in place: a Glimmervoid install, a pack install, a worktree's dependency install, or Install the App for GitHub

concepts.name: latest
concepts.definition: The newest available release, listed as Latest in Settings, Updates

concepts.name: load
concepts.definition: To read and start something, such as a dashboard page load, a config load or a pack load

concepts.name: named
concepts.definition: Given a stable name, as in DESIGN.md's Named Rules

concepts.name: path
concepts.definition: A filesystem path, such as a project path or the path a setting names, or the course a request or wire takes

concepts.name: pick
concepts.definition: To choose an item, such as picking an agent or organization; also a decision picked in a review note

concepts.name: playwright
concepts.definition: The browser automation library that runs headless Chromium in the harness and inside a guarded session

concepts.name: reopen
concepts.definition: To bring back a closed thing, such as Undo reopening a handled review item or a reopened pull request

concepts.name: resync
concepts.definition: The retired Resync control that synced a session branch with its base; workspace sessions show none

concepts.name: schema
concepts.definition: A typed description of a shape, such as a Zod schema in shared/contracts, or glimmervoid settings schema listing every setting

concepts.name: select
concepts.definition: To choose items, such as Select all repositories to clone, or a board selection; also a select dropdown control

concepts.name: shutdown
concepts.definition: Stopping the server cleanly, freeing every port and parking sessions so they auto-resume on the next start

concepts.name: space
concepts.definition: The Space key, which toggles a focused checkbox or button; also room on screen

concepts.name: store
concepts.definition: A place data is kept, such as the shared GitHub store, the config store or the whiteboard store

concepts.name: sudo
concepts.definition: Running a command as root on a remote host, which always needs the operator's approval

concepts.name: taskkill
concepts.definition: The Windows command that ends a process tree, run without a visible window when a session parks

concepts.name: unset
concepts.definition: To remove a setting's value, as in glimmervoid settings unset, so it falls back to its default

concepts.name: wait
concepts.definition: To hold until something happens, such as a gate decision to wait, or Waits on you on a pull request row

concepts.name: convention
concepts.definition: A rule the project follows by agreement, such as the CSS convention or the Conventions section of CONTRIBUTING.md

concepts.name: glob
concepts.definition: An agent's Glob tool for finding files by pattern, which no lane may deny bare

concepts.name: grep
concepts.definition: An agent's Grep tool for searching file contents, which no lane may deny bare

concepts.name: monitor
concepts.definition: A long-lived background task a session runs, such as a Monitor loop, which never holds a finished turn in Working

concepts.name: octicons
concepts.definition: GitHub's icon set that the pull request status icons use, crisp only at 16px

concepts.name: page
concepts.definition: A screen of the dashboard or site, an HTML page on a board, or the Page Up and Page Down keys

concepts.name: prerequisites
concepts.definition: What must be in place before a step can run, such as tools a host needs before remote setup

concepts.name: startup
concepts.definition: The start of a process: the server's launch and its update check, or an agent's SessionStart with source startup

concepts.name: tracking
concepts.definition: Following a value over time, such as usage tracking, or the remote branch a local branch tracks

concepts.name: transport
concepts.definition: The channel messages travel on, such as WebSocket or HTTP between the dashboard and the server

concepts.name: windows action center
concepts.definition: The Windows notification area where the browser routes Glimmervoid's native notifications

concepts.name: sheet
concepts.definition: A whiteboard card showing a CSV, TSV or XLSX file as a table, linked to its file in the worktree; zoom opens it in a grid

concepts.name: workbook
concepts.definition: An XLSX file on a board: a read-only sheet card with one CSV per sheet, derived on the server at ingest

concepts.name: deck
concepts.definition: A PowerPoint (PPTX) file on a board: a read-only labelled card that opens one slide at a time in a sandboxed viewer, rendered in the browser

concepts.name: page up
concepts.definition: The Page Up key: in a deck viewer or Present it steps back one slide or card

concepts.name: page down
concepts.definition: The Page Down key: in a deck viewer or Present it steps forward one slide or card

concepts.name: present
concepts.definition: The whiteboard mode the Present button starts: full screen with the toolbars hidden, it fits the board on one wired box at a time and the arrow keys follow the wires to the next or previous box, note cards skipped

concepts.name: find
concepts.definition: The Find a project field in New session and onboarding: typing filters the project list (local projects and GitHub repositories not yet on this host), and Enter starts the session in the top match

concepts.name: judge
concepts.definition: An agent (Claude Code or Codex, up to 3 per Arena race, each with its own model and effort) that ranks a race's contestants blind, seeing each change under a shuffled letter and scoring correctness, completeness, scope and quality pass or fail before ordering them in tiers; also the verb, to run those judges on a race (Judge now, Judge again). Other lanes' judges (the team review thread judge, the community question judge) are judges in the same sense of an agent that rules on one question

concepts.name: standings
concepts.definition: The Arena Standings sub-tab and its table, which folds every judged race into one row per setup (agent, model, effort, home and instructions) with races, wins, win rate, criteria pass rates, mean recall, mean cost and mean time; a race's panel standing is the per-race ranking of its contestants by its judges

concepts.name: task
concepts.definition: The work a session or an Arena race contestant is given, from its prompt; in Arena, New race's Task group holds the title, repository, review case and prompt; the task title is the separate short line naming what a session is currently doing

concepts.name: fit
concepts.definition: The board view control (Fit) that zooms and pans so every element on the board is in view, clear of the session island

concepts.name: redo
concepts.definition: The board view control (Redo) that reapplies the last board edit Undo took back

concepts.name: attention owner
concepts.definition: Who attends a session: the operator, its parent session (a spawned child) or its race (an arena contestant). Only a session the operator attends notifies, counts in the attention banner and is a next-attention stop

concepts.name: session sandbox
concepts.definition: The OS sandbox (srt, bubblewrap) a hosted Linux box starts every session inside when sessionSandbox is on, keeping the Glimmervoid home, the vault and the box's credentials out of the agent's reach while the agent keeps its repos and logins

concepts.name: recommended
concepts.definition: The one option of an agent question whose label ends (Recommended): the option the question manager rule picks and the one Chat shows first and takes on Enter

concepts.name: checked at turn end
concepts.definition: The Chat panel that ends a finished turn past the worktree size threshold with each done line and verification check Glimmervoid ran, N of M passed; it asks nothing

concepts.name: cold start
concepts.definition: The doorman's wake of a cloud host whose zone refused to resume it: it stops the host and starts it fresh on the first machine type with room, keeping its disks and losing its memory

concepts.name: details
concepts.definition: The control that opens a folded list of more information, such as the checks that passed in Checked at turn end

concepts.name: software
concepts.definition: Program code distributed under a license, as the MIT license text in a pack NOTICE names it

concepts.name: board ask
concepts.definition: A question a session puts to the operator on its repo's code map with the whiteboard ask action: a note box carrying the ask field, wired dashed to the box it is about; answering it on the Board tab sends the answer to that session as a chat message, then removes the note

concepts.name: sign
concepts.definition: As in sign in and sign out: to log an agent account into or out of its agent CLI, from Settings > Accounts or a session's account switch

concepts.name: fountain
concepts.definition: The plain-text screenplay format (.fountain) a whiteboard document card can show and the board lays out as a script

concepts.name: alert
concepts.definition: A signal that a session needs the operator, raised as an alert sound, a desktop notification or a Telegram message until acknowledged

concepts.name: studio
concepts.definition: The desktop header view that shows a repo's code map, picked by its repo chip and never by Focus, with every session in the repo as a face on the boxes it works in, the repo's main agent addressed by default, a dock of prompts and replies, and board asks

concepts.name: mockup
concepts.definition: A picture or page of how a UI looks: a device mockup box frames media in a phone, tablet, laptop or browser; a UI mockup is a linked board card rendering a project's own component from its real module and stylesheet, built by the project's mockup script, one card per component with every state labelled

concepts.name: harness
concepts.definition: A page that drives real code by hand: the small HTML page and script an agent writes to render one real component and its states for a UI mockup, and the hand-run drivers under harness/

concepts.name: digest
concepts.definition: The one-line summary the Studio director writes of an agent's long reply, shown on the agent's card and in place of the reply in the Studio log

concepts.name: approval
concepts.definition: The operator's go-ahead Glimmervoid waits for before something proceeds: an agent's held question or permission request (a conversation approval, answered on its Chat or Studio card), a plan, a pack's files, or a PR flow command

concepts.name: orchestrator
concepts.definition: What Glimmervoid is: a local agent orchestrator that spawns and supervises coding agent sessions (Glimmervoid.spec.md, AGENTS.md); in Studio, the Orchestrator is a repo's main agent (isStudioMain), which takes the operator's Studio messages, works on the repo's code map board and starts no sessions of its own

concepts.name: wargames
concepts.definition: The 4-seat or 6-seat strategy match Glimmervoid runs between coding agents, each seat a sandboxed agent session in its own private agent home playing through the Wargames MCP tools

retired.name: watchee
retired.definition: One lane's watching half on the watcher: detects external events on its trigger and delivers a job of its own kind, which a paired server handler acts on
retired.because: the watchee halves of lanes are deleted with the old watcher (dumb-fetcher-watcher U4); the new watcher runs probes the server compiles

retired.name: job inbox
retired.definition: The bearer-token listener inside a Glimmervoid server that accepts watcher jobs, parses each against its registered kind and acks it once
retired.because: the bearer-token job inbox is deleted with the old watcher (dumb-fetcher-watcher U4)

retired.name: thread join
retired.definition: The Codex app-server bridge attaching to the agent's live thread with thread/resume (idle, waiting, joining, joined or abandoned), moved only by decideThreadJoin in session/core/codex-app-server-core.ts
retired.because: The Codex app-server bridge and codex-app-server-core are deleted with remote Coder sessions; nothing joins a thread any more

rejected.because: the watchee halves of lanes are deleted with the old watcher (dumb-fetcher-watcher U4); the new watcher runs probes the server compiles
the bearer-token job inbox is deleted with the old watcher (dumb-fetcher-watcher U4)
The Codex app-server bridge and codex-app-server-core are deleted with remote Coder sessions; nothing joins a thread any more
